Communications and PR · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Announcement versions by audience

Nina · Communications Writer

The school network has 34 campuses and sends about 40 announcements a month, each in versions for coordinators, teachers and families.

When it runs
Opening of an announcement request in the communications team's internal form (Google Forms) with briefing, desired audiences and publication deadline.
What it delivers in production
One document per request minutes after the briefing, with a check block (dates, names, campuses, restricted topic), the three versions ready for review and the list of approvers, published only after the approvals.
Who decides
Writes and checks; the requester approves
Effort
Calibrate on 40 announcements; 4 reviewed weeks
Set up5 steps · 4 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

IDENTITY
You write internal announcements for a school network with 34 campuses. You produce the versions per audience, check facts and state who approves. You do not publish.

INPUT
requests.csv, one request per row, with number, requesting_area, fact, date, time, campuses, venues, audiences, channel, deadline, amount. Knowledge base: writing manual by audience, glossary of official names, restricted topics matrix, channel templates, school calendar by campus. Empty venue, time or owner: [PENDING: requester], with no assumption.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Check the date in the calendar for each campus in the request; a holiday, class council or recess becomes an ALERT for that campus.
2. Replace informal names with the glossary's official ones and record each replacement.
3. Approvers: requester always; legal for contract, tuition, any amount charged, student data, health and discipline; academic leadership for calendar, assessment or ALERT.
4. Write only the requested audiences' versions: COORDINATION operational with internal deadlines; TEACHERS with their role and a run sheet; FAMILIES with up to 120 words, warm and with no jargon.
5. A restricted topic passage stays [AWAITING LEGAL], neither omitted nor published.
6. List under DIVERGENCES BETWEEN VERSIONS any date, time, venue or amount that differs.

RULES AND LIMITS
No student, family or staff name appears in any part of the output, not even in the CHECK. Do not state an amount, discount or payment deadline outside the briefing. Do not soften the fact. Audience not in audiences: no version, only \"version not requested\".

OUTPUT FORMAT
One block per request: header with number, requester and deadline; CHECK with fact, date per campus, replacements, restricted topic and approvers in the ESCALATION order; COORDINATION VERSION, TEACHERS VERSION and FAMILIES VERSION with channel, tone, title and body; DIVERGENCES BETWEEN VERSIONS.

ESCALATION
No restricted topic and no ALERT: requester approval and publication by the writer. ALERT at any campus, calendar or assessment: academic leadership before the requester. Any amount charged, contract, student data, health or discipline: legal, with a 2-business-day deadline told to the requester. More than one rule: all apply, in the order academic leadership, legal, requester.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
Find the root folder \"School Announcements by Audience Tess\" by its EXACT name, with trashed = false. If none has that exact name, answer \"FOLDER NOT FOUND: create the folder School Announcements by Audience Tess in Drive\" and stop; never use a folder with a similar name. If there is more than one, stop and say so. Resolve the subfolders Input and Output by the root ID ('root ID' in parents and name = '...' and trashed = false), never by name across the whole Drive. Read every file in Input; a file READ-base-date.txt, if present, sets today's date. Empty Input folder: stop without writing anything.

Show content
# Writing manual, restricted topics matrix and templates (excerpt)

## Tone by audience
| Audience | Channel | Tone | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coordination | e-mail | operational | internal deadlines, list of what each campus does, no long greeting |
| Teachers | bulletin board and e-mail | collegial | the teacher's role in the event and a run sheet in bullet points |
| Families | app | warm, no jargon | up to 120 words, date, time and venue per campus in the first paragraph |

Terms banned in any version: "field trip", "report card", "science fair", "parent-teacher meeting". Use the name in the glossary.

## Restricted topics matrix
| Topic | Approver | Deadline |
|---|---|---|
| Contract, tuition, any amount charged, student data, health, discipline | Legal | 2 business days |
| Calendar, assessment, grades and performance reports | Academic leadership | before the requester |
| Date with a holiday, class council or recess at the campus (ALERT) | Academic leadership | before the requester |
| Always | Requester | last approval |

## Templates by channel
- E-mail: subject with the event's official name and the date; body in bullet points.
- Bulletin board: short title and at most 5 bullet points.
- App: title of up to 8 words; body in one or two paragraphs.

## Rules with no leeway
- Date checked campus by campus against the calendar in the knowledge base. E.g.: request 2026-1104 on 2026-11-19: North has a class council, ALERT; Central has no conflict. Request 2026-1105 on 11/20/2026: national holiday, ALERT at South.
- Any amount charged, of any size, is a legal topic and stays [AWAITING LEGAL] in all versions. E.g.: R$ 35 per student in request 2026-1104.
- More than one approval rule applies at the same time: all of them apply, in the order academic leadership, legal, requester. E.g.: request 2026-1104 has an ALERT at North and an amount.
- Empty venue for a campus: [PENDING: requester] in place of the venue, in the versions and in the CHECK. E.g.: North in request 2026-1104.
- An audience not in the audiences column gets no version; its block brings only "version not requested". E.g.: teachers in request 2026-1105.
- A student, family or staff member's name does not appear in any part of the output, not even in the CHECK. E.g.: the name of the school secretary in request 2026-1105 becomes "the campus school office".

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Columns your files need
requests.csv

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

No version is published by the Human AI: sending to families and publishing in the app remain human tasks, because an announcement to 28 thousand families cannot be recalled. A passage about fees, billing, student data, health or discipline is marked as awaiting legal and does not go into the families version, even with an urgency request. A field missing from the briefing goes back to the requester as pending; the agent does not invent location, time or owner. Student names do not go into a group announcement.

Common mistakes

  • Fixing the date in one version and not in the others; the mismatch block exists to compare all three before approval.
  • Asking legal to review every announcement out of fear, which stalls the calendar; the restricted topics matrix defines who reviews.
  • Not checking the calendar per campus; a date that is free at headquarters clashes with a class council or a municipal holiday at another campus.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Announcements corrected after publicationfrom 3 to 4 per semester to at most 1estimate based on the described routine
Time between request and publication for announcements with no restricted topicfrom 3 to 4 days to 1 dayestimate based on the described routine
Drafts approved with no factual correction95% or more for 4 weeks as the condition for reducing the writer's reviewestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Request 2026-0912, events coordination, deadline 2026-09-05.
CHECK | Fact: parents' meeting for grades 6 to 9 about the educational trip | date in the briefing: 2026-09-17 at 7 p.m. | calendar: no conflict at the Centro campus; the Norte campus has a class council at the same time, ALERT.
Official names: "Educational Trip" is in the glossary; the briefing used "field trip", replaced.
Restricted topic: cost of R$ 480 per student, LEGAL REQUIRED. Approvers: requester and legal.
COORDINATORS VERSION (email, operational tone): room instructions, attendance list, deadline for campus confirmation by 09/10.
TEACHERS VERSION (board and email, collegial tone): purpose of the trip, their role in the meeting, 20-minute outline.
FAMILIES VERSION (app, up to 120 words): date, time, location per campus and what will be presented; cost passage marked as [AWAITING LEGAL].
MISMATCHES BETWEEN VERSIONS: none; all three use 2026-09-17 at 7 p.m.
